prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system produces compliant potable water meeting utility targets/demand; boundary: River Intake Pump Station (Ironwood) through Raw Water Screen Channel, treatment/disinfection/storage, High Service Pump Header discharge; distribution excluded.

Ironwood normally operates automatically within withdrawal limits; reduced-capacity service addresses river/equipment/demand constraints. Chief Operator authorizes Storm Intake Mode when normal assumptions fail; staff intensify river/screen/turbidity/pump observation. Pump permissives: adequate suction, discharge path, healthy motor, open isolation valves, no protective trips. Starts blocked by channel downstream low-level limit, drive fault, local control, unproven safety interlock. Lost permissives cause severity-dependent alarm/stop. Temporary manual operation requires Chief Operator authorization, understood cause, observable equipment, acceptable continuity risk.

Raw Water Screen Channel monitors levels/differential, rake/debris status; sends Rake Torque Snapshot after every cleaning cycle. Rising differential indicates blinding/debris; rapid level changes require cleaning/intake-drawdown verification; high-high requires immediate field confirmation.

Quality triggers: turbidity, color, odor, sheen, algae, rapid temperature change. Chief Operator selects pumping adjustment, laboratory testing, downstream monitoring. Laboratory Technician prioritizes abnormal/storm raw-water checks, confirms analyses, reports abnormalities, verifies adjustments; Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench receives process/compliance samples. Coagulant Dosing Skid uses approved feed setpoints; observe closely during rapid turbidity changes. Notify North Filter Gallery and South Filter Gallery of anticipated shorter runs/increased solids; monitor status/headloss/turbidity/backwash.

Chlorine Contact Basin manages disinfection; Chlorine Residual Alarm requires immediate assessment. Clearwell Level Controller coordinates storage; Backwash Recovery Tank supports recovery. SCADA Historian Server (Lantern) retains operating/river/screen/pump/quality trends; controls/instruments/workstations/historian share plant time.

Duty Engineer governs configuration/faults/changes, reviews storm forecasts/river stages; Maintenance Planner coordinates work; Distribution Dispatcher communicates demand; North Distribution Pressure Station and South Distribution Pressure Station influence pumping. Chemical Supplier Driver follows controlled delivery/inventory checks; Residuals Hauler removes residuals/backwash. Trained staff supervise automation, safely intervene, document deviations. External interfaces: power, chemicals, laboratory, residuals, distribution.

New part:
S049: The Distribution Dispatcher is notified when intake limitations could reduce the ability of the High Service Pump Header to meet planned system demand.
S050: The Clearwell Level Controller is watched during intake restrictions because storage level provides the main buffer between reduced raw-water supply and treated-water delivery.
S051: Return to normal service occurs after river level, screen differential, raw-water quality, and pump cycling have stabilized for a period accepted by the Chief Operator.
S052: After a storm event, the Maintenance Planner reviews intake equipment condition and schedules cleaning or inspection work needed to restore reliable operation.
S053: Following a storm-related recovery, control of coagulation and filtration returns to normal only after raw-water quality trends support stable chemical feed and predictable filter loading.
S054: The Chief Operator establishes the starting coagulant dose from recent turbidity, color, alkalinity, pH, temperature, and bench-scale treatment observations.
S055: The Coagulant Dosing Skid, known locally as Marigold, meters the primary coagulant under automatic control during routine operation.
S056: The Coagulant Dosing Skid sends the Alum Batch Ticket when a new chemical lot is placed into service.
S057: Automatic dose trimming is based on analyzer feedback, operator-entered targets, and verified process response rather than on a single instrument value.
S058: When raw-water turbidity changes quickly, the Duty Engineer may authorize a temporary dose adjustment while the Chief Operator confirms the sustained control point.
S059: The North Filter Gallery, known locally as Cobalt, contains a bank of gravity filters operated from the plant control system.
S060: North Filter Gallery records individual filter effluent turbidity and headloss at the end of each control scan.
S061: South Filter Gallery sends the Filter Run Exception Note when a filter run ends outside the normal operating limits.
S062: Filter run management is based on run time, terminal headloss, effluent turbidity, prior backwash quality, and the current condition of upstream treatment.
S063: A filter is not returned to service after washing until rinse-to-waste quality meets the operating target and the turbidity trend is stable.
S064: If a filter shows an unusual turbidity rise, operating staff compare the analyzer trend with nearby sample results before declaring a process upset.
S065: The Laboratory Technician provides confirmation testing when online analyzers disagree with observed filter performance or with routine process samples.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
